case_name: Forrest Crawley and Shawna Crawley v. Commissioner
suitability_reason: Sole decided issue is the amount of a sec. 217 moving expense deduction, resolved by substantiation and a Cohan estimate based on credibility; the 50-mile and 39-week tests were found satisfied without numeric facts.

taxpayer.notes: Wife (UPS employee) transferred from Pennsylvania to Atlanta, Georgia area in late 2015; family moved December 2015.

adjustments: computational adjustments to student loan interest deduction, child tax credit, and adoption credit
conceded: Respondent conceded petitioners are not liable for a sec. 6662 penalty

findings_of_fact.fact: Petitioners claimed a $26,439 moving expense deduction on Form 3903: $25,000 transportation/storage of household goods and $1,439 travel
findings_of_fact.snippet: The Form 3903 reports $25,000 for “transportation and storage of household goods and personal effects” expenses and $1,439 for “travel” expenses.

findings_of_fact.fact: Wife transferred to Atlanta-area workplace between November 16 and December 1, 2015; position changed December 7, 2015
findings_of_fact.snippet: Sometime between November 16 and December 1, 2015, she transferred to a workplace in the Atlanta, Georgia, metropolitan area.

findings_of_fact.fact: Wife's new workplace at least 50 miles farther from former residence than former workplace; employed full time at least 39 weeks in following 12 months
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioners have met their burden of showing that petitioner wife’s new place of employment was “at least 50 miles farther from

findings_of_fact.fact: Wife sold $21,835 of UPS stock on November 23, 2015 to fund move; cash withdrawals of about $12,000 and $8,000 used to pay movers
findings_of_fact.snippet: On November 23, 2015, petitioner wife sold $21,835 worth of UPS stock. Petitioners used the proceeds from this sale to fund their move.

findings_of_fact.fact: Two RV park charges of $530 each paid November 28 and December 28, 2015
findings_of_fact.snippet: Two of these charges were for $530 each paid to Atlanta South RV Park in McDonough
$20,000 for the “mom and pop” moving company; $1,439 for travel expenses; and $530 for lodging.

issues.question: Other (sec. 217 moving expenses): Are petitioners entitled to deduct $26,439 of moving expenses for 2015?
issues.holding: Partially: distance and 39-week tests met; under Cohan, allowed $20,000 movers, $1,439 travel, $530 lodging
issues.computable_reason: Amount rests on Cohan estimate and credibility of testimony; statutory tests found without numeric distances

decision.text: Decision will be entered under Rule 155.
decision.summary: Moving expense deduction allowed in part ($20,000 movers, $1,439 travel, $530 lodging); 6662 penalty conceded by respondent

notes: Deficiency amount not stated in opinion. Derived: allowed total $21,969 (not stated by court). Burden on petitioners. Joint return; petitioners resided in Georgia at filing.
